blockers.title: README quickstart code block is not runnable as pasted
blockers.detail: Copy-pasting the Quickstart snippet into any fresh directory fails at line 4: FileNotFoundError: 'imvigor210_eset.parquet'. The snippet contains no data-resolution; the prose above it says the files 'come from the IOBR data-v1.0 release (or point IOBRX_TESTDATA ... examples/quickstart.py resolves them for you)', and quickstart.py only covers part 1. STOPS a naive copy-paste user at the first line of the advertised quickstart.

blockers.title: Documented data download fails in this environment
blockers.detail: examples/quickstart.py and the full-marker tests fall back to downloading .rda from github.com/IOBR/IOBR/releases; here every attempt dies after ~90 s with http.client.RemoteDisconnected (github.com unreachable; PyPI works fine). Without a local IOBRX_TESTDATA copy the quickstart and the full test suite dead-end. Recorded exactly as encountered; the repo itself documents the IOBRX_TESTDATA alternative, which works.

blockers.title: Plain 'pytest -q' fails on a fresh clone: 13 passed, 11 ERRORS
blockers.detail: pytestmark = pytest.mark.full only MARKS the official tests; nothing deselects them by default (no conftest.py, no addopts). Running the obvious 'pytest -q' from the repo root executes the 11 full tests, which attempt GitHub downloads and error (urllib.error.URLError), rc=1, 147 s mostly spent timing out. The test docstring's 'Enable with: pytest -m full' implies opt-in that does not exist, and the README never gives the working smoke-only command ('pytest -q -m "not full"' -> 13/13 in 10 s). SIGNIFICANTLY MISLEADS a naive user into thinking the test suite is broken.

blockers.title: Documented '--run-full' pytest flag does not exist
blockers.detail: tests/test_parity_official.py docstring: 'pytest -q -m full  # or  pytest -q --run-full'. Actual: 'error: unrecognized arguments: --run-full' (no conftest registers it).
